land.text: Crete: 'a Mycenaean elite clearly ruling Knossos from around 1450 BC'

successors.note: Cliopatria hands Crete over at -1400; the pages date the Mycenaean takeover of Knossos to c. 1450 BC.

capitals.name: Knossos
capitals.note: 'the largest and best-known centre of the Minoan civilisation', not a recorded capital: 'it is unclear whether there was ever a unified Minoan state' and the palaces 'did not primarily serve as royal residences' (Minoan page). Phaistos was the second-largest palace; Kydonia 'the only palatial site in West Crete'.

correction.text: Crete in the First Palace period: the first palace at Knossos 'built around 1900 BC', with Phaistos and Malia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts the Minoans at -1600 but the Knossos page builds the first palace 'around 1900 BC' and the Minoan page has Protopalatial society emerging in MM I (c. 2100-1875 BC) with the first palaces in MM IB (c. 1925-1875 BC); MM II (c. 1875-1750 BC) 'ended with mass destructions generally attributed to earthquakes' and the palaces were rebuilt in MM III. Same extent as Cliopatria's shape. The off-island settlements (Kastri on Kythera, Akrotiri on Thera, Ialysos on Rhodes, Karpathos, Kasos) are traders' colonies and are not drawn.

5,499 km2 (16 grid cells of Crete's 27, bbox 23.6-26.2 E): most of the island, 'the Second Palace period, from about 1700 to 1450 BC, was the height of Minoan Knossos' (Knossos page). No infobox area to compare. The Thera eruption 'occurred around 1600 BC towards the end of the LM IA subperiod'; the page does not draw a Minoan thalassocracy, so the shape stands.

Shape unchanged, but its years should end at -1451: LM IB (c. 1625-1470 BC) 'ended with severe destructions throughout the island' and the page has 'a Mycenaean elite clearly ruling Knossos from around 1450 BC'; the dossier ends -1450 and the Mycenaean Greece dossier takes Crete from -1450, fifty years before Cliopatria's -1400 handover.

region.text: Crete: the first palace at Knossos, 'built around 1900 BC on a hill that had already been occupied for several millennia'

ledger.note: c. 1900 BCE: the first palaces rise on Crete. Knossos page: 'The first palace was built around 1900 BC'; Minoan page: the first palaces date to MM IB (c. 1925-1875 BC). The page gives the palace sites, not a boundary; the whole island is drawn.

region.text: Crete, with 'severe destructions throughout the island' at the end of LM IB and 'a Mycenaean elite clearly ruling Knossos from around 1450 BC'

ledger.note: c. 1450 BCE: the palaces burn and a Mycenaean elite rules Knossos; Crete passes to Mycenaean Greece. Knossos page: 'The palace was partially destroyed around 1450 BC, during a wider period of disruption affecting many Minoan sites' and 'After about 1450 BC, Knossos became an important Mycenaean administrative centre'. Minoan culture 'lasted until around 1100 BC' under Mycenaean rule (LM IIIC c. 1200-1075 BC), as culture, not as a state.

certainty.note: No borders exist: the shape is the island of Crete, drawn as a whole, while 'it is unclear whether there was ever a unified Minoan state'. The coastline is sharp by nature; the question is whether one colour should cover the island at all before the Neopalatial period.

sources.title: Minoan civilization
sources.note: Identity, chronology table (MM IB first palaces, MM II destructions, LM IB destructions, LM II Postpalatial), Thera eruption c. 1600, Mycenaean rule of Knossos from c. 1450, off-island settlements, end c. 1100.

sources.title: Knossos
sources.note: First palace c. 1900 BC, destroyed c. 1700, Second Palace period 1700-1450, partial destruction c. 1450 and Mycenaean administration after, palatial destruction c. 1350.

notes:
Written by the eu-01-a research agent on 2026-10-18 from two pages (budget 1-2).

Start: extended from Cliopatria's -1600 to -1900 with a new keyframe of the same extent, on the Knossos page's 'first palace was built around 1900 BC' (the scope's 'Minoan palaces before 1600 BCE'). The Prepalatial centuries (EM I-III, c. 3100-2100 BC) are not drawn: no palace, no polity.

End: -1450, not Cliopatria's -1401: both pages put the Mycenaean takeover of Knossos at c. 1450 BC; the Mycenaean Greece dossier takes Crete at -1450 (its new keyframe mycenaean-greece_-1450). The LM IIIA-C Mycenaean Crete, and the final palace destruction c. 1350, belong to that dossier.

Type: 'state' although the page doubts a unified state existed; the schema's 'culture' is reserved for pre-3400 BCE. The island is drawn as one colour; a reviewer may prefer palace-level polities (Knossos, Phaistos, Malia, Zakros, Kydonia), which would be new states for batch eu-01-x.

Not drawn: the Minoan settlements on Kythera (Kastri), Thera (Akrotiri, buried by the eruption c. 1600 BC), Rhodes (Ialysos), Karpathos and Kasos, which the page calls colonies or settlements of traders; Thera and Kythera are missing from the gazetteer (listed in the report). The Seshat page gr_crete_new_palace was not opened (budget). No infobox area exists; Cliopatria's 5,499 km2 against the island's roughly 6,800 km2 in this grid is within a factor of two.
